parsed.explanation: Combined regime pairs state-level protections—longstanding gender-identity anti-discrimination and hate-crime coverage, X driver's licences without documentation, covered care and a shield against out-of-state care enforcement—with an operative federal layer the state cannot cancel: binary passport policy, entry screening instructing refusal on sex discrepancy, federal facilities restriction, and documented birth-sex custody harms. Admission and federal encounters are the sharpest traveller-facing exposures; once admitted, state services are comparatively protective but enforcement outcomes for the shield are undocumented.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal policy processes passports only as M/F per supporting documents; cable instructs refusal where documents/records discrepancy casts reasonable doubt on sex, and possible permanent fraud ineligibility if wilful misrepresentation found. Trans athletes barred.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; state driver's licence/ID offers M/F/X on request without documentation, though home passport governs entry.
entry_documents.interaction: State document openness does not control federal border adjudication; discrepancy at entry can precede refusal or additional-evidence demands before any state protection applies.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections policy adopted from 2026 described as cutting hair, removing hormones and substituting psychiatric treatment; immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse. State 2012 case: trans woman held in men's facility, segregated pre-trial, assaulted.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. Petition during 2012 imprisonment led to correct hormone regimen, but no general placement-by-identity protocol documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest or immigration detention moves traveller from protective state services into national/state custody practices documented as birth-sex based and harmful.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: January 2025 executive order barred transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity nationally; some states criminalise use in certain circumstances with first known arrest reported 2025.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division dossier documents no state bathroom ban; state anti-discrimination covers public accommodations since 1993.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State public-accommodations protection does not override federal facilities or other states' bans; traveller remains exposed in federal buildings.

care_services.exposure: National orders target gender-affirming care for minors as 'mutilation', proposed rules would bar public insurance reimbursement under 18, and DOJ subpoenaed hospitals for under-19 records; several orders blocked/enjoined, status contested.
care_services.protection: State public programme covers transgender-related care, insurers barred from excluding it, March-April 2023 orders/law protected care, conversion therapy banned for minors/vulnerable adults.
care_services.interaction: State coverage and shield can protect care obtained in-state, but do not preempt federal investigation, funding or entry consequences; shield enforcement cases not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National guidance uses 'radical gender ideology' in extremist context and 2026 strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' violent groups; 66% poll support for birth-sex document laws cited, indicating majoritarian support for binary documentation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State hate-crime penalties for gender identity since 1993, trans-panic defence abolished 2024, sodomy statute repealed 2023, anti-discrimination since 1993.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State protective law coexists with federal threat-framing and investigation directives; federal actors are not bound by state protections.

minors_guardians.exposure: National executive order directs investigation/prosecution related to teachers facilitating social transition; care for minors nationally targeted, some measures enjoined. State high-school trans athlete policy challenged, outcome not recorded.
minors_guardians.protection: 2023 shield law bars state enforcement of other jurisdictions' warrants/subpoenas/extradition and custody removal over legal gender-affirming care; families travelling for treatment fall inside protection.
minors_guardians.interaction: Shield addresses other-state process, not federal entry, federal investigation or federal custody; minor traveller's protection is therefore state-bounded and untested in decided cases.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific violence figure documented. Airport screening guide notes invasive secondary screening and outing risk. National custody abuse indicates police/custody actors can be perpetrators when detention occurs.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime law, anti-discrimination law and abolition of trans-panic defence are documented legal protections; enforcement data for complaints/charges/outcomes not sourced.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Paper protections without documented enforcement cannot be treated as proven street-level recourse; absence of violence data is not evidence of safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport policy challenged by civil-liberties suit on behalf of seven plaintiffs, unresolved; several executive orders blocked/enjoined; shield law has no documented decided cases; hate-crime/discrimination enforcement not sourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Independent July 2026 assessment places state in most-protective tier; courts have enjoined some national orders and passport litigation is pending.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies depend on which federal measures are in effect at travel time; state remedies do not remedy federal refusal, facilities or custody exposures.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: extended screening, humiliating interview, discretionary refusal/return without routine imprisonment is documented at federal entry. This case is higher than 0.55 because admitted visitors gain state anti-discrimination, care coverage and shield protections not present in the anchor.

Lower than 0.65: that anchor has brief detention followed by apology/compensation and reliable court-ordered release. Here federal refusal instruction, facilities ban and custody abuse are systematic, and no documented remedy restores entry or placement.

Higher than 0.35: that anchor has routine exclusion with almost never-granted appeals and no protective internal regime. Here state law is materially protective for services/care and imprisonment/execution for being trans is not documented, so severity is lower.

parsed.synthesis: The operative journey is sequential: federal border and federal facilities/custody first, protective state law second. State protections materially improve housing, services, care access and shield against other-state care enforcement for admitted travellers and families, but they do not cancel federal document screening that can refuse entry, federal facilities restriction, or birth-sex custody harm if detained. Minors gain state shield protection for in-state care yet remain exposed to contested national targeting of minor care. That interaction—real state protection bounded by an active federal hostile layer—places the case just below the 0.65 anchor, at 0.58.
